thread:
Sam: Running into weird behavior with the Python SDK async tool/function calling + structured output. Token refresh seems to retrigger the request and the tool on the model side is invoked twice in some runs. Anyone seen this?

Maya: Can you paste a small snippet? are you using RedwoodAsyncClient or Client.from_token?

Sam: Minimal repro:```python
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(token=my_token) as client:
    resp = await client.chat.create(
        model="gpt-xxx",
        messages=[{"role":"user","content":"call tool"}],
        tools=[my_tool],
        tool_call=True,
        response_format=MySchema,
    )
```
Behavior: if the auth token is close to expiry the SDK triggers a refresh during the request and I observe two outgoing requests to the service. Server-side the tool is executed twice and I get two tool outputs stitched back; client typing sometimes shows Optional[List[MySchema]] which is confusing.

Liam: Which HTTP lib? httpx? aiohttp? That sounds like a double-retry layer (http client + SDK). Also, streaming + structured parsing can cause weirdness if the parse consumes a response that gets retried.

Sam: We're on httpx.AsyncClient. Traces show two distinct requests with different auth timestamps. Workaround was to set sdk retry=0 and refresh token manually before the call, but that's not acceptable for end users.

Ana: I remember a bugfix for sync clients similar to this — async path might have been missed. I'll look through recent PRs. @Maya any thoughts on structured output coercion interacting with retries?

Maya: Hypothesis: request is sent, the server executes tool, then token refresh happens while response streaming/parse is ongoing; SDK decides to retry the request and sends it again without idempotency, causing server-side tool to run twice. For structured output, the parser may also convert/merge both outputs into a list which explains the Optional[List[MySchema]] typing artifact. We need either idempotency keys for tool calls or ensure retries don't replay side-effectful tool invocations.

Sam: I can reproduce reliably on a token that expires in-flight. I also noticed my editor (pyright/mypy) shows the response type as Union[List[MySchema], StructuredParseError] in some cases. Maybe stubs are not reflecting the coercion behavior.

Liam: Can you share the HTTP trace/headers (no secrets) and a tiny repro? I can try to write a test that simulates token refresh mid-request.

Sam: Pushed a tiny gist with sanitized traces: https://gist.github.com/sam/repro-token-retry (contains request ids and headers). Also pasted a minimal trace snippet: ```
-> POST /v1/chat  Authorization: Bearer token_old
<- 401 token_expired
refresh token
-> POST /v1/chat  Authorization: Bearer token_new  x-retry: 1
<- 200 tool_executed
```

Ana: I'm opening an issue (bug, high) with the repro and linking the gist. From runtime side we can add an idempotency-key header for tool invocation envelopes so retries don't re-run side effects.

Maya: Also we should add unit tests for async streaming + structured output parsing under retry. And fix typing: update stub so response type reflects that parser returns a single coerced object (or raises StructuredParseError) rather than union list noise.

Sam: I'll try a small patch to inject an X-Idempotency-Key into the request envelope for tool calls and run the repro. If anyone from infra wants to look at the token refresh sequencing that would help too.

Liam: I can take the test and add it to pipeline. Thanks for the repro, Sam.

deploy-bot: incident: token-refresh-retry spikes detected in dedicated-prod around 12:34 UTC. Noted correlation with SDK v0.12.3.

Sam: Thanks all. Happy to help iterate on the fix and the typing changes.

Maya: Filed PR checklist: ensure async and sync parity, add idempotency header, update typing stubs, add tests for streaming+retry. Will post PR number once opened. :thumbsup:
